newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan seeks to reduce SABIC 5-year MTBE term deal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seeks to reduce SABIC 5-year MTBE term deal.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) is negotiating with industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) to renew a term contract for methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) for one year instead of five, a CPC official said on Thursday.
The official said SABIC officials visited Taiwan on July 21 to renew the term contract for three cargoes of 3,500-tonnes of the octane enhancer per month -- a third of CPC's annual needs.
The current five-year contract expires at the end of this year.
The CPC official said SABIC wanted a three-year term deal at least.
"We only want a year-by-year contract," the official told Reuters. "From next year, local requirement is not so clear."

CPC plans to introduce 98-Ron petrol next year and Formosa could start to sell its own gasoline products as part of government plans to open up the energy sector and reduce CPC's monopoly position, which made CPC uncertain over future demand.
Taiwan currently consumes the 95-unleaded and leaded, and 92-octane unleaded grades.
Taiwan's gasoline consumption totals 9.0 million kilolitres, which was expected to rise to 11.0 million by 2000, a source at giant petrochemical group Formosa Plastics said.
But a trader said CPC was also looking at other potential MTBE sources in the future, which might preclude a five-year term contract with SABIC.
"The main reason why CPC wants to cut the term is because their joint-venture plant in Qatar will commence in 1999 and they will have a surplus," a trader said.

CPC has a 20-percent stake in the Qatar Fuel Additives Company (QAFAC) project with 50-percent owned by Qatar's General Petroleum Corp, and 15-percent each by Taiwan's Lee Chang Yung Corp and Canada's International Octane Ltd.

The plant, located in Messied near Doha, is projected to use 100 million cubic feet per day of gas and 500,000 tonnes- per-year (tpy) of butane to produce 610,000 tpy of MTBE and 830,000-tpy of methanol from mid-1999.
Last year, a CPC official said the state company planned to stop importing by 1999 and would source its MTBE from QAFAC. It could even have some available for export, the official said.

CPC currently covers its MTBE requirments from SABIC through the five-year term contract, from Italian producer Ecofuel through a six-month (July-December) term for up to four cargoes, and through monthly spot tenders for up to two cargoes, the official said.
It also takes 150,000-200,000 tpy from private Taiwanese producer Tasco. CPC does not have any interest in the plant but supplies the butane feedstock.
CPC's potential rival Formosa plans to start up a naphtha cracker in 1998 -- the first phase of a US$9 billion refinery and petrochemical complex.
A CPC official said Formosa was planning to enter the domestic gasoline retail market when the cracker is onstream.
But a Formosa source said the government had not decided yet whether Formosa would qualify for marketing gasoline.

He said by 2000, when the refinery is commissioned, Formosa would be able to produce 6.5 million kilolitres a year (112,000 barrels-per-day) and the company aimed to take 40-percent of the Taiwan market.
-- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3086)
